description: Showcase of strong saved model analyses. Relative clauses, clitics, classifiers and sentence-final particles. Each case is an exact copy of a saved analysis that passes the invariant sweep, the contract warnings, the offline visual and camera audits and the right-to-left mirror check without an exception.

cases.description: Japanese prenominal gap relative with a null operator, the は topic moved to the topic edge and an adjectival predicate with tense.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/71-ja-relative, analysis 1 of 1. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/71-ja-relative.
cases.sentence: 太郎が読んだ本はおもしろい。

derivationStages.stageRecord: Externally merge a silent nominal operator with 読んだ, forming a head-final verbal object. The operator receives the verb's Theme role and represents the book understood as the thing read. This analysis uses a null-operator relative clause rather than moving the pronounced noun 本 out of the clause. 読んだ is introduced as an already inflected verbal terminal bearing past tense; its internal morphological derivation is not represented. Repeated category labels mark the objects produced by Merge, without an independently stipulated bar-level template.
derivationStages.statement: The relative-clause verb combines with its unpronounced object operator.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the proper nominal 太郎 with the following case particle が. Merge a silent agentive v with the existing verbal object, then merge 太郎が as its external argument. The resulting head-final structure places the subject before the object position and the pronounced verb. The subject receives the Agent role from the verbal complex. The presence of が records the subject's nominative requirement; its licensing by finite T is established in the next stage.
derivationStages.statement: 太郎が is merged as the relative clause's external argument.

values.exponence: Past tense is pronounced within 読んだ; T has no separate exponent.

values.representation: A moved operator with a trace at its original object position.

values.interpretation: Abstraction over the Theme of reading.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge silent past T above the verbal structure. T licenses the nominative subject 太郎が and agrees in tense with the already inflected verb 読んだ; no additional past-tense exponent is pronounced. Next merge a silent relative C and internally merge the object operator at its edge. The earlier object position is now represented by a silent trace, while the operator retains its identity at the landing site. The operator binds that trace, abstracting over the thing that Taro read. The relative subject remains in its externally merged position: this analysis does not impose obligatory subject raising in Japanese.
derivationStages.statement: The finite relative clause is completed by operator movement.

values.interpretation: The noun denotes a book satisfying the property of being read by Taro.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the completed relative clause to the left of 本, with N providing the label of the resulting nominal object. The relative property restricts the noun: the relevant book is something Taro read. The noun is therefore associated with the operator's variable without being a movement copy of that operator. Merge a silent referential D and the following topic particle は. This analysis treats は as a nominal-edge topic marker whose clausal licensing will be established at the topic edge. Separately merge おもしろい with a silent predication head, then merge the book nominal as the subject of that predication. The adjective assigns its property to that nominal. No overt copula is introduced because the input uses the Japanese inflecting adjective directly as its predicate.
derivationStages.statement: The relative clause modifies 本, and the resulting nominal enters the matrix predication.

values.exponence: Nonpast tense is pronounced within おもしろい; T has no separate exponent.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge silent finite nonpast T above the matrix predication. Its tense is realized by the inflected adjective おもしろい, with no independent tense word or copula. The book nominal is still in its predication-subject position in this workspace, establishing the source required for the subsequent topic movement. The relative clause retains its own past T, so the reading event is past while the matrix assessment is nonpast.
derivationStages.statement: The matrix adjectival predication receives finite nonpast tense.

values.representation: A moved subject topic with a trace in its predication position.

values.interpretation: The book Taro read is the topic; being interesting is predicated of it.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent Top above the finite matrix clause and internally merge the entire は-marked book nominal at its edge. The moved nominal retains its internal relative clause and its pronounced topic marker; a silent trace now occupies its previously established predication-subject position. This is a movement analysis of the subject topic, not a hanging-topic analysis with an independently generated null pronoun. Top licenses は and establishes the nominal as the topic of the comment おもしろい. Merge a silent declarative C above the topic structure to complete the root clause. The pronounced order is 太郎 が 読んだ 本 は おもしろい, exactly the input apart from punctuation and spacing.
derivationStages.statement: The は-marked subject moves to the matrix topic edge, completing the sentence.

cases.description: Swahili class-7 relative pronoun in Spec-CP with relative concord, a pro subject and copular ni.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/78-sw-relative, analysis 1 of 1. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/78-sw-relative.

relations.relation: Finite licensing of a null subject

values.morphologicalAnalysis: ni-: first-person singular subject; -li-: past; -som-: read; -a: final vowel
values.syntacticCommitment: one inflected V terminal, not four independently positioned syntactic terminals

derivationStages.stageRecord: The sentence means ‘The book which I read is good.’ The analysis uses DP, NP, CP, IP and AP projections. Kitabu heads the subject's NP under a phonologically null D. In the relative clause, ambacho is an overt class-7 relative pronominal DP, initially merged as the complement of nilisoma. The verb assigns that DP its internal Theme role and, under government, accusative Case. The reader is a silent first-person singular pro, base-generated in Spec-IP in this GB analysis; the verb's external theta-role is assigned to this subject through its predication domain. Finite I licenses pro with first-person singular agreement and nominative Case. A lexicalist treatment inserts nilisoma as an already inflected verbal word: ni- expresses first-person singular subject agreement, -li- past tense, -som- the reading predicate, and -a the final vowel. These morphological components are not independent syntactic terminals. The relative C, matrix copula ni, and adjectival predicate kizuri remain separate objects. The matrix copula will be analyzed as an invariant I head selecting an adjectival predicate, not as a lexical verb requiring a further VP.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the nominal subject, the relative clause before movement, and the matrix predicate.

values.representation: pronounced landing head and silent V trace

values.phonologicalEffect: none; nilisoma was lexically inflected before movement

derivationStages.stageRecord: The previously established V head nilisoma raises into the immediately governing finite I head. Its landing occurrence retains the overt word, while a silent V trace occupies the complement-taking verbal position. The raised V and the original abstract I form a complex I head. This local head movement links the lexical verb's past and first-person singular inflection to the corresponding features of I; it does not create or respell the word. The earlier theta and Case assignments remain associated with the verbal chain. In particular, ambacho is still in its original object position at this stage, so its subsequent A-bar movement will have a separately represented source.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the finite relative-clause verb from V to I.

values.representation: overt relative operator and silent DP trace

values.binding: the operator A-bar-binds the object variable
values.case: accusative, inherited from the object position
values.emptyCategoryLicensing: object trace properly governed through the verbal head chain
values.interpretation: the property of being an entity that I read
values.locality: clause-internal movement with no intervening bounding CP or island
values.thetaRole: Theme, inherited from the object position

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative C takes the existing IP as its complement. Ambacho then moves from the object position displayed in the preceding workspace to Spec-CP, leaving a silent DP trace. The pronounced relative pronoun is therefore a phrasal operator in Spec-CP, not the C head itself. Its A-bar chain binds the object variable and receives its Theme role and accusative Case through the original object position; no second theta-role or Case is assigned at the landing site. The movement is clause-internal and crosses no intervening CP boundary or island. The object trace is properly governed through the verbal head chain, and the operator binds it from Spec-CP. The resulting clause denotes the property of being something that the speaker read.
derivationStages.statement: Form the relative CP and move ambacho to Spec-CP.

values.antecedentLink: the relative object variable ranges over the book restriction
values.attachment: right adjunction of CP to NP inside DP

values.distinction: noun-class concord with the book, not subject agreement with the reader

derivationStages.stageRecord: The completed relative CP is right-adjoined to the book NP, producing an outer NP containing the earlier NP and the relative modifier. This makes Kitabu ambacho nilisoma one DP rather than a matrix noun followed by an independent clause. The nominal restriction and the relative property combine so that the understood object of reading is the book denoted by the subject. Kitabu is noun class 7, and the relative concord in ambacho, including -cho, identifies that same class. This concord links the nominal antecedent with the relative operator; it is distinct from the first-person singular agreement that licenses the reader pro inside the relative clause.
derivationStages.statement: Attach the relative clause as a restrictive modifier inside the subject DP.

values.structuralCommitment: no matrix lexical VP and no matrix V-to-I movement

values.derivationalCommitment: subject base-generated in matrix Spec-IP; no additional small-clause raising
values.thetaLicensing: external argument of the adjectival predication

values.interpretation: goodness is predicated of the book, not of the embedded reader

derivationStages.stageRecord: The invariant copular I ni combines with AP kizuri as its complement, and the completed book DP occupies matrix Spec-IP. On the selected nonverbal-copula analysis, ni supplies the finite copular link without introducing a lexical VP or undergoing V-to-I movement. Its matrix use here has the ordinary present interpretation and licenses nominative Case on the subject. The AP predicates goodness of the book DP and licenses that DP as its external predication argument; the subject is base-generated in Spec-IP rather than raised from an additional silent small clause. The class-7 ki- of kizuri agrees with the class-7 head kitabu across the intervening relative modifier. Consequently, the adjective describes the book, not the first-person subject of nilisoma. The final pronounced terminals are Kitabu ambacho nilisoma ni kizuri, with the relative object trace, verbal trace, pro, null D and abstract functional material remaining silent.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix copular clause and its adjectival predication.

cases.description: Greek integrated clitic doubling with the proclitic in a clitic head above T and a pro subject.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/17-el-clitic-doubling, analysis 1 of 2. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/17-el-clitic-doubling.

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines the article τον with the proper name Γιάννη. The article and name concord in masculine singular accusative features. The resulting definite nominal is merged as the complement of είδα and receives its internal-argument interpretation. A silent transitive light verb introduces the null first-person singular subject and licenses accusative on the object. Labels on branching objects identify their projecting heads; they do not introduce independently stipulated bar levels. In this analysis, τον Γιάννη is the verb's integrated object, not a right-peripheral discourse constituent.
derivationStages.statement: Build an integrated transitive predicate with an overt definite object and a null subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge raises είδα from the previously established verbal position and adjoins it to the transitive light verb. The landing occurrence retains pronunciation; the lower verbal copy is silent. The subject and integrated object remain in their original argument positions. This first head-movement step supplies the complex head that can subsequently raise to finite T.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the lexical verb to the light-verb head.

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent finite T is externally merged above the light-verb domain. T agrees with the accessible null subject in first-person singular features and licenses its nominative Case. T contributes finite past interpretation; the lexical form είδα already supplies the Greek aorist, perfective form rather than being decomposed into independently pronounced tense and stem terminals. The subject and verbal complex have not yet moved to T's domain.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce finite past T and establish subject agreement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verbal complex already present at v raises to T, leaving a silent copy of the whole complex. Independently, the previously established null subject internally merges at the edge of T's projection, leaving a silent lower subject copy. These movements can share a stage because neither requires the other's result. This analysis adopts an EPP requirement satisfied by null pro; it does not infer an overt preverbal subject from the surface order. Only the highest lexical-verb occurrence is pronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Move the verbal complex to T and satisfy the subject-position requirement.

values.thematicCommitment: one internal argument, realized by the integrated nominal

derivationStages.stageRecord: A preverbal clitic head Τον is externally merged above T's projection. Under the agreement-head analysis adopted for this reading, it doubles the integrated accusative object: the clitic and τον Γιάννη share masculine singular reference, but the clitic receives no separate thematic role. This is a doubling dependency, not movement of the object nominal or of its article. The clitic is phonologically dependent on the finite verbal host, yielding the Greek proclitic order Τον είδα. A silent declarative C closes the clause. The pronounced terminals now yield exactly Τον είδα τον Γιάννη. The object remains within the predicate, allowing an integrated discourse-given-object reading without requiring a right-dislocation boundary.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the integrated clitic-doubling clause.

cases.description: French faire causative: the causee is marked by à and the lower theme clitic climbs to the finite causative verb.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/39-fr-clitic-climbing, analysis 1 of 3. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/39-fr-clitic-climbing.
cases.sentence: Jean le fait lire à Marie.

derivationStages.stageRecord: This analysis yields ‘Jean makes Marie read it.’ Externally merge lire with the pronominal argument le, establishing the theme relation. Separately merge à with Marie. The resulting oblique nominal will enter the lower external-argument position, rather than a recipient position selected by lire. Category labels identify projections of their heads; no independent phrase-structure templates are assumed.
derivationStages.statement: The accusative clitic is the theme of lire; à Marie will identify the reader.

values.linearization: the reduced predicate precedes its external argument

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent nonfinite v with the VP, then externally merge the oblique nominal as its external argument. Marie is consequently the reader, not the addressee of reading. This analysis adopts a right-linearized external-argument position in the reduced French faire-infinitif complement. Bare Phrase Structure does not itself require every specifier to precede its sister; the rightward ordering here is a construction-specific linearization commitment, not an unrecorded movement.
derivationStages.statement: Marie is introduced as the lower agent.

values.condition: the lower predicate has a syntactically represented theme

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the causative head with the reduced nonfinite predicate. Faire establishes a causative dependency whose lower agent is Marie. Under clause union, the lower theme receives accusative and the overt causee receives dative, expressed by à. Then externally merge Jean as the causative head's causer. The form fait is entered as the finite lexical exponent; its present-tense and agreement features will be licensed by T. Introducing that exponent now does not claim that it is already in its final position.
derivationStages.statement: Faire introduces Jean as causer and licenses the transitive causative case pattern.

values.operation: Internal Merge of Caus with T
values.pronunciation: the higher occurrence is pronounced; the lower occurrence is silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent finite T above the causative phrase. T agrees with Jean, licensing nominative and third-person singular agreement, and licenses the present indicative exponent fait. Internally merge the previously represented causative head with T; its lower occurrence becomes silent. The resulting complex head contains pronounced fait and an unpronounced T. There is no intervening syntactic head between Caus and T in this analysis.
derivationStages.statement: Finite T attracts faire and agrees with Jean.

values.operation: Internal Merge to the finite clitic position
values.pronunciation: the higher occurrence is pronounced; the lower occurrence is silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge le from the object position of lire as a left-adjoined clitic on the finite head. The reduced causative complement permits this dependency across the infinitive: le is pronounced before fait although it receives its thematic interpretation from lire. The source occurrence becomes silent. This is clitic movement, not a new object of faire.
derivationStages.statement: The lower theme clitic climbs to the finite head.

values.operation: Internal Merge to the TP edge
values.pronunciation: the higher occurrence is pronounced; the lower occurrence is silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge Jean from the causative external-argument position at the edge of TP, satisfying T's subject requirement. Pronounce only its higher occurrence. The completed tree spells Jean le fait lire à Marie: Jean is the causer, le is what is read, and Marie is the person made to read. The infinitive remains nonfinite, and its overt external argument remains in the construction's postinfinitival dative position.
derivationStages.statement: Jean raises to the finite subject position, completing the causee reading.

cases.description: Cantonese stacked sentence-final particles (未 for the question, 呀 for discourse) in C heads, with V-to-Asp 食咗.
cases.source: GPT-6 Astra, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/04-yue-sfp, analysis 1 of 1. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/04-yue-sfp.

relations.relation: Complement selection and internal theta-role assignment

values.configuration: The lexical verb governs its NP complement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: 食 selects the bare NP 飯 as its complement, assigning it the Theme role. 飯 can denote rice or a meal without requiring different syntactic structures. The third-person pronoun 佢 is generated in Spec-VP and receives the Agent role from the verbal predicate. 食 governs its complement and assigns it structural accusative Case. The analysis uses NP for nominal arguments, a VP-internal subject, and separate functional heads for perfective aspect, finite inflection, interrogation, and discourse force. These heads remain independent syntax objects at this stage. 佢 does not grammatically specify the referent's gender.
derivationStages.statement: Build the transitive VP and establish its thematic and object-Case relations.

values.temporalCommitment: 咗 does not by itself assign past tense.

values.morphology: No overt tense or agreement exponent is introduced.

values.interpretation: Whether the person has eaten rice or a meal by the relevant reference time, or has not yet done so.
values.questionType: polar question with a not-yet alternative

values.contribution: Addressee-oriented conversational tone over the polar question.
values.surfaceOrder: 未 precedes 呀 because the discourse projection contains the interrogative projection.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Perfective 咗 takes VP as its complement, establishing an aspectual description of the eating event rather than an inflectional past tense. A phonologically null finite I projects above AspP; using finite I to license the eventual subject is the GB implementation adopted for this Cantonese clause, not a claim that Cantonese has overt agreement. The subject is still in Spec-VP, and Spec-IP has not yet been filled. Right-headed interrogative C, realized as 未, takes IP and asks whether the perfective proposition holds by the contextually relevant reference time, contrasting it with the not-yet alternative. Thus 未 is not analyzed as a preverbal negative head negating 食. This analysis encodes the alternative in interrogative C and does not posit an unpronounced coordinated negative clause. The higher, also right-headed, discourse C 呀 takes the interrogative CP and adds an addressee-oriented conversational tone. Their nesting accounts for 未呀 rather than 呀未. These functional relations are established before either movement operation.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the aspectual and clausal projections, including the two ordered final particles.

values.chainInterpretation: The silent V trace preserves the lexical position relevant to theta assignment and object government.
values.linearization: 食 precedes 咗 within the derived head.
values.locality: Asp is the next higher head; no intervening head is crossed.

derivationStages.stageRecord: 食 moves from the V position displayed in the preceding workspace and left-adjoins to the immediately higher aspectual head 咗. The pronounced verb occurrence retains its identity at the landing site, while a silent V trace occupies its former position. The resulting complex head contains 食 followed by 咗. This local head movement crosses no intervening head and leaves a head chain through which the verb's previously established thematic and object-government relations remain available at its base position. The analysis therefore derives the postverbal placement of 咗 syntactically, rather than treating 食咗 as an unanalyzed lexical verb. The subject remains in Spec-VP at this stage, making the workspace preceding subject movement explicit. No special written realization is needed: the lexical terminals 食 and 咗 directly supply their characters in 食咗.
derivationStages.statement: Move 食 to Asp and derive the verb–perfective complex 食咗.

values.licensing: The raised subject satisfies the clausal subject requirement and locally binds its A-trace.

values.configuration: Finite I licenses the subject in Spec-IP.

values.bindingStatus: The pronoun has no local coindexed antecedent and is locally free.
values.reference: Its referent may be supplied by the discourse.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject NP 佢 moves from the previously displayed Spec-VP position to Spec-IP, leaving a silent NP trace. This is local A-movement to a non-theta position: the subject retains the Agent role associated with its VP-internal origin and receives no second theta role. Its landing position satisfies the clausal subject requirement. Finite I licenses nominative Case on the raised NP in the adopted GB analysis. The resulting A-chain has one theta position and one Case position; the subject c-commands its trace without an intervening subject. The pronominal 佢 is free in its local binding domain, IP, satisfying Principle B; a discourse antecedent remains possible but is not syntactically supplied by this sentence. The verb remains in Asp, with no additional movement to I or C, because the overt aspectual combination and the final interrogative head already account for the sentence's ordering. Pronounced terminals now give 佢 食 咗 飯 未 呀, exactly the input apart from ignored spacing and punctuation. The completed question means approximately 'Has that person eaten rice/a meal yet?' The rice-versus-meal interpretation and the pronoun's contextual reference do not create additional syntactic parses.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the subject to Spec-IP and complete 佢食咗飯未呀？

cases.description: Turkish prenominal object relative with the nominalizing participle and possessive agreement, and a suffixal past copula.
cases.source: GPT-6 Astra, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/76-tr-relative, analysis 1 of 1. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/76-tr-relative.

relations.relation: Nominal inflection licenses the relative subject

values.emptyCategory: referential pro licensed and identified by nominal agreement

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative clause underlying Okuduğum contains the transitive verb oku ‘read’, a silent first-person singular subject, and a silent object operator. In this GB analysis, the subject originates in Spec-IP and the object occupies the complement position of V. The verb assigns its reader role to the subject and its theme role to the object; it governs the object position and licenses abstract accusative Case there. The nominalizing tense participle -DIK and first-person singular possessive agreement -Im are represented as components of a complex nominal I head. This head licenses the silent subject through agreement and assigns it genitive Case, corresponding to the overt alternative benim ‘my/I-GEN’. The operator remains in its argument position at this stage. The suffix notation is abstract: vowel harmony, consonant alternation, and collective surface realization have not yet been established. The temporal interpretations ‘that I read’, ‘that I have read’, or contextually ‘that I was reading’ do not require different constituent structures.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the head-final nominalized relative clause before movement.

values.chainInterpretation: argument structure and object government are preserved through the verbal trace
values.locality: V moves to the immediately higher I

operations: intervocalic k-to-ğ alternation in the participial suffix

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb moves from the previously represented V position to the adjacent governing I head, adjoining on its left and leaving a silent head trace. This local V-to-I movement creates the head-final order verb–participle–agreement; the original inflectional head remains inside the resulting complex head. The verbal chain preserves the predicate's argument relations and government of the object position. After head movement, morphological realization applies to oku, -DIK, and -Im together: suffix harmony and the intervocalic alternation of the participial consonant produce Okuduğum. The realization association records that written form without replacing the retained lexical and suffix representations.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the relative verb to nominal I and establish Okuduğum.

values.dependency: operator locally A′-binds its object trace
values.locality: clause-internal movement without an intervening island

relations.relation: Prenominal relative modification and external-head linkage

values.headAnalysis: external head linked to the object variable
values.interpretation: book that the first-person singular subject read

derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent relative C selects the nominalized IP. The silent object operator moves from its established V-complement position to Spec-CP, leaving an NP trace. The operator locally A′-binds that trace; its chain receives the theme role and abstract accusative Case at the source, and crosses no intervening clause or island. The resulting head-final CP is adjoined to the left of N′ headed by kitap ‘book’, producing the Turkish prenominal relative construction. The external noun is linked to the operator's variable, so the book is understood as what the speaker read, not as the reader. This is an external-head operator analysis: kitap has not moved out of the relative clause. An NP analysis is used without positing an overtly unsupported determiner; contextual definiteness does not introduce a separate structural reading.
derivationStages.statement: Form the object relative and attach it prenominally to kitap.

relations.relation: Matrix finite Case tense and agreement

derivationStages.stageRecord: The completed nominal occupies the matrix Spec-IP position, where the adjectival predicate güzel ‘beautiful’ assigns it the bearer-of-property role through copular predication. This traditional GB implementation base-generates the matrix subject in Spec-IP rather than deriving it by movement from an additional small clause. Matrix I contains the copular base i, past -DI, and silent third-person singular agreement. Finite I licenses nominative Case on the matrix NP and agrees with it; that matrix Case is independent of the embedded operator chain's accusative and the relative subject's genitive. A silent declarative C selects the matrix finite IP. The adjective remains in AP: this analysis does not posit A-to-I movement. Copular attachment and its written realization are reserved for the following stage, so the independently represented predicate and inflection are visible before that operation.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the matrix adjectival predication and past copular inflection.

relations.relation: Suffixal copular attachment and surface realization

values.copularRealization: no independent copular vowel in the suffixal form
values.operation: postsyntactic attachment of copular inflection to the adjacent adjective
values.syntacticCommitment: AP remains in situ; no A-to-I movement

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix copular inflection is phonologically attached to the immediately preceding adjectival predicate. In this suffixal realization, the copular vowel has no independent segmental exponent and past -DI harmonizes as -di after güzel, yielding güzeldi. This is a postsyntactic realization commitment, not movement of the adjective or a change in its category. Consequently the syntactic workspace is unchanged, but a separate final stage is necessary to establish the surface association only after the predicate and copular inflection have been assembled. The earlier Okuduğum association remains in force. Together with the independently pronounced noun kitap, the two associations yield the exact input. The completed structure expresses ‘The book that I read was beautiful’; contextual differences in the relative clause's temporal interpretation leave the operator dependency and matrix predication unchanged.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the surface realization of Okuduğum kitap güzeldi.
